meal.workflow_md:
## T-Minus Timeline
TimeAction
T-5 hrBake olive oil cake (HTML: cool and hold uncovered at room temperature)
T-3 hrPrep all vegetables and salad components (HTML: keep salad vegetables refrigerated and undressed)
T-2 hr 45 minBegin stew — render bacon, brown wings (deeply)
T-2 hr 05 minBegin reduction phase
T-1 hr 35 minStew enters oven with wings, bacon, potatoes, early carrots
T-1 hr 05 minAdd thighs and remaining carrots
T-35 minBegin raising oven to 400°F / 205°C — stew has ~15 min remaining (HTML: and tolerates gradual oven rise at this stage)
T-30 minMake gremolata (max 30 min hold; discard and remake if longer); hold in small uncovered bowl
T-20 minStew exits oven; remove aromatics, reclaim wing meat, season with vinegar and salt; hold uncovered
T-15 minToast bread once oven confirms 400°F / 205°C
T-5 minDress salad; final seasoning check on stew
TPlate stew + ~½ tsp gremolata per bowl; bread and salad to table. Serve immediately.
## Failure Prioritisation *First failure if delayed: bread crust softens, then stew thickens. Dessert fully decoupled.* ## Workflow Notes *Critical path: wing browning → reduction → final thigh braise (HTML: wing browning → reduction → first oven phase → thigh braise → final seasoning). Protect these above all else; bread and salad yield to stew timing — do not delay stew service for either component. If timing slips: serve stew immediately, toast bread after plating, dress salad at table.* *Oven sequence: Cake (350°F / 177°C) must complete before dinner. Stew owns oven at 325°F / 163°C. Raise to 400°F / 205°C at T-35; transition takes ~15–20 min; the stabilized braise tolerates this drift. Bread enters only once temperature is confirmed. Dutch oven owns primary burner throughout stew.* ## Holding Chain
ComponentHold StrategyMax HoldDriftCorrective
StewDutch oven, uncovered, off heat20 minThickensLoosen with hot broth
SaladUndressed, refrigerated2 hrSoftens once dressedDress only before service
BreadLoose rack hold15 minCrust softensRe-toast 3–4 min
CakeRoom temp, uncovered8 hrMinimal driftNone
GremolataSmall bowl, uncovered30 minZest dulls; garlic sharpensDiscard and remake

dishes.name: Fennel, Celery, and Herb Salad with Lemon Vinaigrette
dishes.source: Recovered from chicken-stew-sunday.docx (menu dated Sunday 25 May 2026; HTML render chicken-stew-sunday.html dated 26 May 2026 used to fill gaps)
dishes.summary: Thinly shaved fennel and celery tossed at the last moment with parsley leaves and a deliberately broken lemon-olive oil vinaigrette, with optional shaved Parmesan at the final toss.
dishes.method_md:
## Dish Overview *Raw fennel, celery, and parsley against the stew's soft profile — crunch, freshness, and acid.* HTML: A crisp, acidic raw salad that cuts through the stew's collagen-rich body. ## Yield & Timing *Serves 6–8 · 20 min active · No cook* (HTML: Total: 20 min · Active: 20 min) ## Prep Phase 1. Shave fennel thinly. Slice celery thinly. Refrigerate until service. ## Active Cooking 1. Whisk lemon juice + olive oil + salt + pepper vigorously. Broken vinaigrette is intentional (a lightly broken vinaigrette). ## Holding & Assembly 1. Dress immediately before serving. Toss with parsley. Add Parmesan at final toss if using. ## Critical Control Points
SeverityFailure Mode & Sensory CueRecovery
MajorDressing too early — fennel softens and releases waterUnrecoverable for texture; salad remains edible
## Adjustment Notes *Adjust: increase lemon if stew is especially rich. Adjust salt after adding Parmesan.*

dishes.name: Chicken Stew with White Wine, Wings, and Gremolata
dishes.source: Recovered from chicken-stew-sunday.docx (menu dated Sunday 25 May 2026; HTML render chicken-stew-sunday.html dated 26 May 2026 used to fill gaps)
dishes.summary: Boneless chicken thighs braised uncovered at 325°F in a base built from rendered bacon, deeply browned wings and an aggressively reduced wine-broth-soy-anchovy fond, thickened with a butter-flour roux, with split-timed carrots and small red potatoes, finished with sherry vinegar and a parsley-lemon-garlic gremolata.
dishes.method_md:
## Dish Overview *Deep chicken flavor through browned wings, staged reduction, and oven braising. Gremolata and sherry vinegar restore brightness at service. The reduction phase is essential — do not shorten it.* HTML: A deep chicken stew with wing collagen, staged reduction, aromatic lift, split carrot timing, and fresh gremolata. ## Yield & Timing *Yield: 6–8 · Total: ~2 hr 45 min · Active: ~50 min · Oven: 325°F / 163°C* ## Prep Phase 1. Heat oven to 325°F / 163°C. 2. Pat wings dry thoroughly. 3. Season thighs with ¾ tsp Diamond Crystal kosher salt + black pepper. Temper 15–20 min. 4. Divide carrots into two equal portions. ## Active Cooking *Critical path: wing browning → reduction → final braise. (HTML: wing browning → reduction → first oven phase → thigh braise. Do not shorten reduction.)* ### Phase 1 — Render Bacon and Brown Wings 1. Cook bacon (in the Dutch oven) over medium-low until browned, 6–8 min. Transfer to bowl. 2. Increase to medium. Brown wings deeply 10–12 min total. Brown in batches if necessary. 3. Cue: deep golden brown, crisped edges, dark fond on pot. Transfer wings and bacon to bowl. Hold room temp up to 30 min. ### Phase 2 — Build and Reduce Base 1. Add onion, celery, garlic, anchovy paste, thyme. Cook 3–5 min. 2. Add wine, 1 cup / 240 ml broth, soy sauce. Scrape up all browned bits. 3. Add bay leaf, parsley stems, lemon peel. 4. Boil aggressively until nearly dry, 12–15 min. Cue: vegetables begin lightly frying in concentrated fat; liquid glossy and nearly evaporated. Do not stop early. ### Phase 3 — Build Stew 1. Reduce to medium-low. Stir in butter. Add flour; cook 1 min, stirring continuously. 2. Gradually whisk in remaining 4 cups / 960 ml broth until smooth. 3. Add wings, bacon, potatoes, and first half of carrots. Bring to simmer. 4. Transfer uncovered to oven for 30 min. ### Phase 4 — Add Thighs 1. Remove from oven. Scrape fond above liquid line back into stew. 2. Add thighs and remaining carrots. Return uncovered to oven for 40–50 min. 3. No pull temperature — thighs remain submerged to service. 4. Primary cue: paring knife slides through thickest thigh with no drag on entry or exit; thigh fibers separate cleanly under light pressure. If resistance remains: 10 more min. 5. Observation: late carrots should remain intact while tender. ## Holding & Assembly 1. During final 30 min: make gremolata in small uncovered bowl. Max hold 30 min; discard and remake if longer. 2. Remove and discard bay leaf, parsley stems, lemon peel. 3. Remove wings; reclaim meat from flats and drumettes. Discard bones, skin, cartilage. Return meat to stew. 4. Stir in 1–2 tsp sherry vinegar. Taste after first teaspoon before adding the second. 5. Adjust salt and pepper. 6. Hold uncovered off heat up to 20 min. Loosen with hot broth if stew thickens. 7. Serve with ~½ tsp gremolata per bowl. ## Critical Control Points
SeverityFailure Mode & Sensory CueRecovery
CriticalIncomplete reduction — vegetables still floating in abundant liquid with no sizzleContinue reducing until vegetables lightly fry in fat
MajorAdvancing with pale wings and weak fond — wings pale with little fond on potContinue browning before proceeding to Phase 2
MajorOver-thickened stew — coats spoon heavily like gravyThin gradually with hot broth
MajorOvercooked late carrots — collapsing at edgesCarrot texture lost; stew remains acceptable
MinorExcess gremolata — lemon/garlic dominates aromaReduce garnish on remaining bowls
## Adjustment Notes *Adjust: add second tsp vinegar only if stew still tastes heavy. Adjust salt after vinegar. Thin with hot broth if over-thickened. Increase gremolata to brighten a dense bowl.*

dishes.name: Toasted Country Sourdough
dishes.source: Recovered from chicken-stew-sunday.docx (menu dated Sunday 25 May 2026; HTML render chicken-stew-sunday.html dated 26 May 2026 used to fill gaps)
dishes.summary: Thick-cut country sourdough brushed with olive oil, toasted 8–10 min at a confirmed 400°F / 205°C after the stew exits the oven, and finished with flaky salt.
dishes.method_md:
## Dish Overview Thick slices of country sourdough brushed with olive oil and toasted in the 400°F oven once the stew has exited, finished with flaky salt. ## Yield & Timing *Serves 6–8 · 5 min active · Oven: 400°F / 205°C after stew exits* (HTML: Total: 15 min · Active: 5 min) ## Prep Phase 1. Slice thickly. Brush with olive oil (HTML: brush lightly). ## Active Cooking 2. Wait for oven to confirm 400°F / 205°C (full temperature recovery) before bread enters. Toast 8–10 min. 3. Cue: edges crisp and browned; centre yields under firm pressure without feeling rigid. ## Holding & Assembly 4. Hold on loose rack up to 15 min. Re-toast 3–4 min if crust softens. ## Critical Control Points
SeverityFailure Mode & Sensory CueRecovery
MinorOvertoasting — deep brown edges, rigid centrePartially recoverable with extra olive oil. Reduce time next batch.

dishes.name: Orange Olive Oil Cake
dishes.source: Recovered from chicken-stew-sunday.docx (menu dated Sunday 25 May 2026; HTML render chicken-stew-sunday.html dated 26 May 2026 used to fill gaps)
dishes.summary: A one-bowl 9-inch orange olive oil cake — zest rubbed into 200 g sugar, three eggs, 180 ml extra-virgin olive oil, milk and orange juice folded with 210 g flour — baked 40–50 min at 350°F, cooled 20 min, held up to 8 hr and dusted with powdered sugar.
dishes.method_md:
## Dish Overview *Citrus lift and restrained sweetness to close the meal; soft crumb contrasts the crisp bread and gremolata earlier.* HTML: A soft citrus olive oil cake that resets the meal with orange aroma and restrained sweetness. ## Yield & Timing *One 9-inch cake · Serves 8 · Active: 20 min · Oven: 350°F / 177°C · Bake before dinner* (HTML: Total: 1 hr 30 min) ## Prep Phase 1. Heat oven to 350°F / 177°C. Grease 9-inch cake pan (HTML: prepare with neutral oil or olive oil; line base with parchment and lightly oil parchment). ## Active Cooking 2. Rub orange zest into sugar. Whisk in eggs. 3. Add olive oil, milk, and orange juice. 4. Fold in flour, baking powder, and salt. Do not overmix (fold only until dry flour disappears; stop before batter turns elastic). 5. Bake 40–50 min. Cue: centre springs back lightly; skewer with moist crumbs, no wet batter. Continue in 5-min increments if wet batter remains. ## Holding & Assembly 6. Cool 20 min before unmolding. If cake resists: return to pan, cool 10 min more. 7. Hold uncovered at room temp up to 8 hr. Serve with light powdered sugar. ## Critical Control Points
SeverityFailure Mode & Sensory CueRecovery
MajorUnderbaked centre — wet batter on skewerContinue baking in 5-minute increments
MinorExcess mixing — batter becomes thick and elasticFold minimally; stop once flour is just incorporated
## Adjustment Notes *Adjust: reduce powdered sugar if serving after wine. Add fresh zest at serving for more citrus aroma.*
